record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Extend 3D bipedal locomotion modeling and control to robots or prosthetic systems with spherical or otherwise nontrivial foot shapes, and determine how to achieve gait stability when passive or active prostheses are present. This includes the open 3D case of spherical feet and the broader question of stable locomotion with prosthetic components inspired by the rolling behavior of the human ankle-foot system.

evidence.quote: The 3D case is open and interesting.
It would be interesting to extend this work to address gait stability in the presence of passive or active prostheses.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system with continuous single-support phases governed by Lagrangian dynamics and discrete impact maps at foot contact. Suppose the feet are not flat point-contacts but instead have a nontrivial geometry — in particular, spherical feet that roll on the ground during the single-support phase, producing additional unactuated rotational degrees of freedom (rolling in both sagittal and frontal planes) and thereby higher-degree underactuation than the planar case.

(a) Develop a hybrid dynamic model and a feedback-control design (for instance, in the spirit of virtual constraints and hybrid zero dynamics) for such a 3D biped with spherical feet, and prove the existence of an exponentially stable periodic walking gait. Specifically, exhibit a controller under which the restricted Poincaré return map of the hybrid zero dynamics has all eigenvalues strictly inside the unit disk.

(b) Extend the framework to a biped (or human-robot hybrid) in which one or both lower limbs are replaced by a prosthetic component — passive (purely mechanical, no actuation) or active (with one or more actuators) — whose foot interacts with the ground through a rolling contact mimicking the human ankle-foot complex. Provide conditions on the prosthesis design, the controller of the intact limb (and of the active prosthesis when applicable), and the gait parameters under which an exponentially stable periodic 3D walking gait exists.
artifact.category_tag: Hybrid systems and bipedal locomotion control
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent literature has investigated 3D bipedal walking with curved/spherical feet and hybrid zero dynamics, and separately prosthesis control, but a complete framework giving provably exponentially stable 3D walking gaits with spherical feet and with passive/active prostheses through rolling foot contact does not appear to have been fully established; controlling 3D bipeds with multiple degrees of underactuation remains acknowledged as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Models, Feedback Control, and Open Problems of 3D Bipedal Robotic Walking
status_evidence.snippet: For 3D robots with more than one degree of underactuation, not much is known.
status_evidence.claim: 3D underactuated bipedal walking control is identified as a largely open problem.

status_evidence.title: Optimized 3D stable walking of a bipedal robot with line-shaped massless feet and sagittal underactuation
status_evidence.snippet: Stable 3D walking with line-shaped feet under sagittal underactuation.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for nontrivial (line-shaped) feet, but not spherical feet in full 3D.

status_evidence.title: Bipedal Model and Hybrid Zero Dynamics of Human Walking With Foot Slip
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid zero dynamics extended to foot-slip / nontrivial foot interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Related extensions exist but the spherical-foot 3D and prosthesis case is not fully resolved.
